visitsPerYearByCategory.citation: Stand-in visit counts for the GSS answer categories, an assumption registered with SG-P15-closeness-model: almost daily as five a week, once or twice (or several times) a week as two a week, several times a month as two and a half a month, about once a month as twelve a year, several times a year as four, about once a year as one, never as none.

gss.citation: General Social Survey 1972-2024 Cumulative Datafile, Release 3 (SDA codebook): how often the respondent spends a social evening with parents (SOCPARS), a brother or sister (SOCSIBS) or relatives (SOCREL); percent of all valid answers, pooled years. The rest of each parents and siblings row is "no such people" (29.1% and 9.2%); means are taken over the seven listed categories only.

gaps: Opening closeness uses the average visit rate for the tie, not each pair's own history of visits.
Relatives outside the town make no decisions, so they never start contact themselves.
Old classmates have no opening closeness until someone makes contact; time at school is counted only for classmates still in school together (part 3).
